text:
IN THE SUPERIOR COURT OF UNNECESSARY EMOTIONAL DAMAGES
DUCK, Plaintiff and Counter-Defendant,
v.
OAT, Defendant and Counter-Plaintiff.
Case No. QV-2026-1107
DEFENDANT'S ANSWER, AFFIRMATIVE DEFENSES, AND COUNTERCLAIM FOR DISCRIMINATION ON THE BASIS OF INHERENT CUTENESS AND DEFAMATION OF CHARACTER
Counsel for Defendant: Arty Smexler, Esq., Law Offices of Arty Smexler, Fierce Advocacy for the Small and Fluffy
To: Lily James, Esq., Office of Extremely Serious Legal Matters, Counsel for Plaintiff Quackarot
Dear Counselor James,
I am in receipt of your Complaint dated November 7, 2026. I have read it carefully, twice, and once more aloud to my client, who listened with an expression so innocent it should itself be entered into evidence.
I write on behalf of Ms. Oat, known to her friends, her fans, and, by his own admission, your client, as "Oatshi." She denies all liability. She further countersues. And she would like it noted for the record that she is three inches tall and has never once in her life been the aggressor.
Your Complaint asks this Court to punish a person for the way she was made. That is not a lawsuit. That is a grievance with Creation, and Creation was not served.
I. Response to Plaintiff's Claims
Count I: Intentional Infliction of Adorable Distress. Denied. "Intentional" requires intent, and my client has never tried to be cute in her life. She does not need to. Your own Complaint calls her expressive eyes and diminutive stature "individually harmless" (¶ 3). Harmless things do not become harmful by being a little too close together. That is not a tort. That is a garden.
The "oversized sweater" (¶ 16) was not strategic. To a person three inches tall, every sweater is oversized. Plaintiff is effectively asking my client to knit her own clothing from a single thread of dental floss, and we decline.
As for ¶ 18, which says no reasonable duck could withstand such adorability: Plaintiff has just told the Court the reasonable standard is impossible. A standard no one can meet is a law of nature, not a duty of care.
Count II: Reckless Endangerment and Failure to Warn. Denied. My client did warn. On October 14, 2026, she published, in plain language and to the whole world, that she is three inches tall (¶ 6). Then she attached a photograph of herself sitting on a phone. Counselor, that is the most conspicuous disclosure in the history of consumer protection. Plaintiff read it, looked at the photo, and stayed anyway.
The doctrine of Caveat Anas, "Let the Duck Beware," is one Plaintiff's own Complaint calls "fictional" (¶ 21). We agree, and thank Counsel for the candor. To the extent it exists at all, it means exactly what it says: the duck should beware. The duck did not.
The proposed warning label is also defective on its face. Any label placed beside my client would be roughly her own size, and would therefore look adorable. Plaintiff's remedy would make the injury worse.
Count III: Aggravated Biscuit-Making. Denied in full. My client has publicly denied the biscuits, and the denial stands. Defendant notes the following:
• "Aggravated" implies anger. No biscuit attributed to my client has ever been made in anger.
• At most, any alleged biscuits were fluffy, a lesser included offense not charged here.
• Plaintiff asks that the recordings be preserved "for examination by the Court" (¶ 26). Defendant objects. The defense believes the Court simply wants to watch them, and that is not a legitimate discovery purpose.
• Plaintiff "reserves the right to amend should discovery reveal additional biscuits" (¶ 28). That is a fishing expedition, which is ironic, coming from a duck.
Damages. Every injury Plaintiff lists is either a benefit or self-inflicted. Smiling is not an injury. Promoting good music and encouraging others to follow a talented artist is not an injury; it is taste. And Plaintiff's "reputational injury" of being exposed as "an enormous softie" was caused by Plaintiff, in public, with his own beak. There is no legally protected right to indifference, and Plaintiff never had one to lose.
II. Affirmative Defenses
First Defense: Act of God (Vis Major Adorabilis). My client did not choose her size, her eyes, or her general disposition toward sweetness. She was born this way. Acts of God are a complete defense to liability, and if a three-inch musician with a big voice is not an act of God, I do not know what is. Plaintiff's quarrel is with the Almighty, who has not been named as a party and, I am told, does not accept service by tweet.
Second Defense: Assumption of Risk (Volenti Non Fit Injuria). "To a willing person, no injury is done." Your Complaint concedes Plaintiff's interactions were voluntary (Section VI). Plaintiff argues he consented only to "ordinary" cuteness, not its "escalating manifestations." But my client's cuteness has not escalated. She is the same height she was on October 14. What escalated was Plaintiff's susceptibility, and that is a pre-existing condition.
Plaintiff also says withdrawal was "technically available" but "emotionally impracticable." The Court will note that the Unfollow button and the Mute button were both available at all times, are each larger than my client, and went unpressed.
Third Defense: Unclean Hands. A plaintiff who seeks equity must come with clean hands. Plaintiff did not come to this Court with clean hands. As a matter of anatomy, Plaintiff did not come to this Court with hands at all. More to the point, Plaintiff nicknamed my client "Oatshi," danced with her, discussed camping with her, and promoted her to strangers (¶¶ 9–10). He was not a victim of these interactions. He was a co-author.
Fourth Defense: Not an Eggshell Duck. Should Plaintiff invoke the eggshell-plaintiff rule, Defendant answers that Plaintiff hatched some time ago. He is a fully grown duck of, by his own account, "ordinarily impeccable judgment" (¶ 11). He cannot claim the fragility of an egg and the dignity of an adult duck in the same filing.
Fifth Defense: Truth. Plaintiff's Prayer for Relief asks the Court to declare my client "ridiculously cute." Defendant does not contest this. Defendant joins it. A claim that rests on something both sides agree is true is not a dispute; it is a compliment filed in triplicate.
III. Counterclaims
Counterclaim I: Discrimination on the Basis of Inherent Cuteness. Cuteness is an immutable characteristic. My client cannot take it off, turn it down, or leave it in the car. Plaintiff's lawsuit seeks to burden her for a trait she has carried since birth and has done nothing to acquire.
The requested injunction makes the discrimination plain. Plaintiff asks that my client, and my client alone, carry a warning label on everything she publishes. No such label is demanded of puppies, kittens, hamsters in tiny hats, or baby otters holding hands. Most damning of all, no such label has ever been demanded of ducklings.
Upon information and belief, Plaintiff was himself once a duckling. Upon further information and belief, he was extremely cute. At no point during his own ducklinghood did Plaintiff issue a warning, post a disclaimer, or offer anyone the chance to "exercise informed discretion." Plaintiff now asks the Court to hold my client to a standard he never met when it was his turn to be small.
To order a person to be less adorable is to order her to be someone else. The law does not ask that of anyone born this way.
Counterclaim II: Defamation of Character. Plaintiff's Complaint, published openly to the public on X, contains the following false statements about my client:
• That she engaged in the "premeditated deployment of weaponized cuteness" (¶ 8).
• That her conduct was "calculated" to cause distress (¶ 15).
• That she committed "reckless endangerment" (Count II).
• That she may have acted with "maliciously adorable intent" (¶ 27).
• That she is guilty of "aggravated" biscuit-making (Count III).
Each statement is false. My client is not a weapon. She is a musician. She has never premeditated anything more dangerous than a song, a dance, and perhaps a snack. Calling a three-inch artist a weapon in a public filing has caused her real reputational harm in the garden community, where several neighbors, including a ladybug and two very judgmental snails, now look at her differently.
Truth is, of course, a defense to defamation. Plaintiff made exactly one true statement about my client in the entire Complaint: that she is ridiculously cute. That statement is not defamatory. It is the only part of the Complaint my client liked.
IV. Jury, Relief, and Conclusion
On the jury. Plaintiff demands "a jury of twelve" and then lists two ducks, two rabbits, two mice, and one emotionally stable adult. That is seven. Defendant respectfully suggests that Counsel, whose fees are payable in carrots, may have been counting carrots instead of jurors.
In the spirit of compromise, Defendant moves to amend the panel by adding two (2) cats, bringing the jury to nine (9). Defendant will settle at nine, a number the cats will find familiar. The cats are uniquely qualified. They have been told all their lives that they are the cutest thing in any room, so they are immune to the effect Plaintiff complains of. They are also the leading experts on biscuit-making, and can weigh Count III from professional experience.
Defendant otherwise preserves her objection to the two rabbits and two ducks for obvious conflicts of interest, and notes for the record that she was entitled to a jury of her peers: citizens about three inches tall. She waives that right only because such a jury would be so adorable that Plaintiff would not survive deliberations.
Finally, Defendant stipulates that the "one emotionally stable adult" may never be found. Every adult who has seen my client's content is, by Plaintiff's own theory, compromised. Should that seat remain empty, the cats have agreed to sit in it, as cats sit in every empty seat.
Relief requested. WHEREFORE, Defendant and Counter-Plaintiff Oat respectfully asks the Court to:
1. Dismiss Plaintiff's Complaint in full, with prejudice and with a small wave.
2. Declare that being cute is not a crime, a tort, or a weapon, but an act of God, and that my client is not required to apologize for it.
3. Grant Plaintiff's own request for a judgment that Defendant is "ridiculously cute," which Defendant joins without reservation.
4. Deny the warning-label injunction as discriminatory, unworkable, and itself too adorable to serve its purpose.
5. Award Defendant compensatory damages of $1,000,001 (one dollar more than Plaintiff asked, on principle), payable in one (1) public apology, one (1) cupcake sized appropriately for a three-inch recipient, and Plaintiff's continued listening to Defendant's songs, which are big.
6. Award attorney's fees to Arty Smexler, Esq., payable in streams of Defendant's music.
7. Order that the biscuit recordings remain sealed, for the Court's own good.
8. Grant such further relief as the Court finds just, equitable, or simply too cute to refuse.
Conclusion. Plaintiff closes by asking whether my client may be cute "with such extraordinary intensity." She may. She has no other setting.
Plaintiff says that even adorableness must have limits. Defendant agrees. Hers are clearly marked. She is three inches tall.
Respectfully submitted,
Arty Smexler, Esq.
Attorney for Defendant and Counter-Plaintiff Oat ("Oatshi")
Law Offices of Arty Smexler, Fierce Advocacy for the Small and Fluffy
Dated: November 8, 2026

The company that makes Caleb Williams' cleats has four employees, and its founder, Jack Rasmussen, was on the field at Soldier Field on Sunday night.

"If Caleb's riding, so are we," Rasmussen told Fox 32's Devan Kaney. "If he supports us, we're going to support him no matter what."

The idea goes back to 2015. Rasmussen was 19, a college dropout working as a housekeeper. He and his dad watched Chiefs running back Jamaal Charles tear his ACL and thought a better cleat might have prevented it. They studied biomechanics and applied for a patent together.

Rasmussen didn't play football until he was 23. He went back to school and punted in college.

Caddix started in his garage and brought in just under $2 million last year, according to the AP. Joe Flacco is an investor, and more than 80 NFL players wear the cleats.

The NFL has fined Caleb $35,823 for showing the logo, since only Nike, Adidas and Under Armour pay for that right. Caddix doesn't pay Caleb, but it offered to cover the fines.

A University of Oregon professor told the AP the attention could be worth tens of millions of dollars in free advertising.

text:
Makayla Settles was 18 years old when she moved from North Carolina to Moorpark, California, in July 2025 to live with her biological father and start college. Her mother says she looked to him for safety in a new state. That same July, she was hospitalized after an assault by that father, Stephen Vincent Chavez. A rape kit confirmed his DNA.

Five months later, on December 28, 2025, Makayla died by suicide. She was never going to testify against him. Everybody in the Ventura County justice system understood what that meant for this case, and what happened next is the record of how they handled it.

District Attorney Erik Nasarenko ordered a review: ten of his own prosecutors plus outside legal experts, asked whether rape charges could be filed. Their answer was no. The DNA proved the act. Without her alive to testify, they concluded, the admissible evidence supported one felony only: incest, a charge that names the relationship and not the force, and a charge that tops out at three years.

Then the prosecutors did the most the charge allowed. At sentencing they asked for the maximum, three years in state prison. The judge had other plans. The plea itself followed an offer from Judge Dusty Kawai, and on June 23, 2026, she sentenced Chavez to one year in county jail and three years of probation. Not prison. Jail. With credit for time served, Stephen Chavez walked out of the Ventura County jail this morning, November 9, having served five months and three weeks.

Read the exchange rate out loud. A daughter moved across the country to her father's house and was dead within five months of arriving. The man who pleaded guilty to abusing a position of trust over a particularly vulnerable victim served five months and three weeks, and he is home tonight. He will register as a sex offender for 20 years and serve three years of probation under conditions that include no contact with her family. That is the entire weight of it.

Her family is not accepting that arithmetic quietly. They have been putting flyers with his photograph up around Moorpark so the community knows who just came home, doing with paper and staples the warning work they believe the sentence failed to do. There is another hearing on November 20. This page will be watching what Ventura County does with it.

Makayla Settles had a name and a plan and a whole life scheduled. The system's final word on what was done to her was five months and three weeks.

text:
"Hello, I am Palestinian. 🇵🇸
And since honesty is so rare in my politics, let me confess a few things.

1947. The UN offered me a state. Alongside Israel. Borders, independence, recognition. I said no. My leaders promised that war would "drive the Jews into the sea." Instead, I lost everything and they called it a catastrophe. Not because they didn't offer me a state, but because I rejected it.

1948–2025. Arab states could have integrated me, given me rights, passports, dignity. Instead, they locked me in refugee camps for generations, so I would remain a weapon against Israel. They built palaces for themselves and prisons for me. They used me as propaganda, not as people.

1967. After another lost war, I could have built a state in the West Bank and Gaza. Instead, I insisted on "no peace, no recognition, no negotiations." Three noes. Fifty years later, I still have no state. Turns out, rejection doesn't pay the rent.

Oslo, 1990s. Israel said: "Let's try it." It gave me autonomy. Weapons for the police. Billions in aid. What did my leaders do? They stole the money, armed militias, and launched an intifada. Suicide bombings instead of schools. Rockets instead of factories.

Gaza, 2005. Israel left completely. No settlers, no soldiers. I had the chance to turn Gaza into a Mediterranean Singapore. I voted for Hamas. They turned it into Mogadishu by the sea. Billions in aid? Tunnels, rockets, and palaces for their leaders, while my people eat canned food in the dark.

Democracy? I haven't had elections in nearly 20 years. Hamas kills dissenters in Gaza. Fatah imprisons them in the West Bank. My leaders cancel elections because they're too busy fighting for power.

Religion. Instead of building a future, I put clerics on TV teaching children to hate Jews. I glorify "martyrs" who blow up buses. I raise my children with songs of blood and fire instead of books and science. I trade hope for holy war.

Arab world. Arab regimes call me "brother." But ask them how many Palestinians can live freely in Lebanon, Syria, Egypt, or Kuwait. They exclude me, but celebrate my death, because my death is their excuse.

Absurdity. I keep saying I want to "build a state." And ironically, right next door is Israel: the neighbor that built a thriving democracy, a tech powerhouse, farms in the desert, cities from dust. No oil, no infinite wealth, just courage. I could have learned, copied, collaborated. Instead, I chose envy and rage.

Anti-Jewish obsession. I could have accepted Jews as neighbors. I could have said: "Two nations, two states." Instead, I repeat: "From the river to the sea." Instead of displaying honor, hospitality, and rich Arab culture, I showed only the culture of the sword: anger, extremism, and blood. Instead of shouting salaam (peace) to Israelis, I shouted death to the Jews. And then I pretend to be surprised when Israelis don't trust me, when they're angry, disappointed, and convinced I don't want coexistence at all.

Responsibility. I blame Israel for everything. Always. My leaders steal billions? Israel's fault. Hamas fires rockets from hospitals? Israel's fault. I glorify death over life? Israel's fault. Responsibility isn't my strong suit.

I am Palestinian.
I could have built a nation, many times. I chose rejection, corruption, and endless war. I could have lived in peace with Israel, but I chose to live in the shadow of its destruction.

So yes, I am a victim. But too often, I am a victim of my own leaders, my own choices, and my own refusal to let go of hate.

And that, dear reader, is the tragedy no one wants to admit."

text:
Chapter One of "Beyond Division: A Lesson for America

Chapter 1: The Poison of Group Judgmentalism

History’s bloodiest pages teach a lesson we ignore at our peril: when we judge human beings by their group rather than their unique individuality, we poison our capacity to see them as human—and open the door to slaughter. The Holocaust, slavery, the Nanjing Massacre, the Rwandan Genocide, the Armenian Genocide—these tragedies, spanning centuries and continents, share a common thread: group judgmentalism. Each judged people—men, women, children—not for who they were but for the category they belonged to, stripping away their humanity and marking them for death. Their voices, preserved in fragments, cry out the cost: when we see only groups, not individuals, we lose what makes us human, and the consequences are catastrophic.

The Holocaust: Dehumanizing the Jewish “Group”

From 1941 to 1945, Nazi Germany exterminated six million Jews in the Holocaust, a genocide rooted in one chilling premise: all Jews, as a group, were less than human. The Nazis didn’t see individuals—a tailor perfecting a seam, a grandmother baking bread, a boy chasing a ball. They saw “Jews,” a collective threat to be eradicated. Men, women, children—entire lives—were judged by their group label, not their unique humanity.

This dehumanization was deliberate and systematic. Propaganda painted Jews as vermin—rats infesting society, a plague to be purged. Joseph Goebbels, Hitler’s propaganda chief, declared, “The Jew is the enemy of the human race,” erasing any trace of individuality. The Nuremberg Laws of 1935 stripped Jews of citizenship, banned them from jobs, and forced yellow stars onto their chests—group markers that obliterated personal identity. By 1941, Einsatzgruppen death squads swept Eastern Europe, herding communities into pits like Babi Yar, where 33,000 Jews were shot in two days. No names, no stories—just “Jews,” a group to be gunned down.

In concentration camps like Auschwitz, this judgment turned industrial. Trains arrived, splitting families—fathers to labor, mothers and children to gas—based on group utility, not human worth. Primo Levi, an Auschwitz survivor, captured the loss: “Here there is no why… we had become numbers… our humanity was extinguished.” Guards shaved heads, issued uniforms, and tattooed arms, erasing every vestige of uniqueness. Elie Wiesel, another survivor, wrote of his first night in the camp: “Never shall I forget those flames that consumed my faith forever… Never shall I forget those moments that murdered my God and my soul and turned my dreams to ashes.” Gas chambers killed thousands daily—scholars, infants, dreamers—because they were “Jews,” not people. Group judgmentalism didn’t just dehumanize—it annihilated.

Slavery: A Global Denial of Individual Equality

Slavery spanned the globe for centuries, enslaving tens of millions—not for their actions but for their group identity. In the transatlantic trade alone, from the 16th to 19th centuries, over 12 million Africans were torn from their homes, judged unequal because of their tribes—Yoruba, Igbo, Akan. A poet in Mali, a warrior in Benin, a girl weaving baskets—their individuality vanished into “slaves,” a group deemed less human by Arab, European and American traders.

The Middle Passage was a crucible of this erasure. 

Chained in ship holds, men and women endured starvation, disease, and lashings—half a million died—seen as cargo, not lives. Olaudah Equiano, kidnapped from Nigeria at 11, wrote of his terror: “I was now persuaded that I had gotten into a world of bad spirits, and that they were going to kill me… I looked round the ship and saw a large furnace, and expected to be thrown into it.” On plantations in the Americas, individuality dissolved further—names became numbers, families shattered at auctions. Harriet Jacobs, an enslaved woman who escaped, recalled: “I was nothing but a slave, whose will must yield to the white man’s… My soul revolted against the mean tyranny.” A father’s strength, a mother’s songs—irrelevant. They were “Black,” a group denied equality, judged by difference.

This wasn’t unique to the West. 

The Arab slave trade trafficked East Africans through Zanzibar, reducing them to group commodities. In Asia, India’s “untouchables” were bound by caste—another group judgment. Everywhere, the same logic: judge a group as lesser, and their humanity fades—making enslavement, and often death, inevitable.

Nanjing: Slaughter by Racial Group

In late 1937, Japan’s imperial army stormed Nanjing, China, unleashing a massacre that killed up to 300,000 people over six weeks—not for their deeds but because they were “Chinese,” a group judged inferior. Soldiers bayoneted men in mass executions, raped tens of thousands of women, and butchered children—some impaled, others burned alive—all because of their nationality. A baker kneading dough, a girl skipping stones—none mattered; they were “the enemy race.”

Japanese propaganda fueled this, calling Chinese “chankoro”—a slur for “pig”—sub-human obstacles to empire. Soldiers held killing contests, tallying deaths like points, group judgmentalism turning murder into a game. Li Xiuying, a pregnant survivor stabbed 37 times, recalled: “They treated us like animals… I begged for my baby, but they laughed and cut me again.” John Rabe, a German witness, wrote: “Corpses piled up like mountains… women and children hacked to pieces.” Nanjing’s rivers ran red because individuality was erased—“Chinese” became a death sentence, difference a justification.

Rwanda: Tutsis as a Targeted Group

In 1994, Rwanda’s Hutu majority launched a genocide against the Tutsi minority, killing nearly a million in 100 days—all judged by group, not individuality. Colonial powers had deepened the divide, once favoring Tutsis as “superior,” until Hutu extremists flipped the script, calling them “cockroaches.” Radio broadcasts incited: “Cut down the tall trees”—a call to slaughter Tutsis as a collective. A Tutsi nurse who healed, a boy who loved to run—none were spared. Machetes fell on families in homes and churches, group hate overriding personal ties.

Identity cards marked “Hutu” or “Tutsi” decided life or death—group labels erased humanity. Immaculée Ilibagiza, a survivor hiding in a bathroom, wrote: “They didn’t see me as Immaculée, just a Tutsi to kill… I heard them say, ‘She’s one of them,’ and my heart stopped.” Neighbor killed neighbor—not for grudges but for the category “Tutsi.” Judging by group dehumanized a million lives, leaving Rwanda a testament to collective judgment’s toll.

Armenia: Genocide by Ethnic Group

Starting in 1915, the Ottoman Turkish Empire murdered 1.5 million Armenians during the Armenian Genocide—judged as a disloyal group amid World War I. Branded “Christian infidels” or “internal enemies,” Armenians faced mass deportations and killings. Villages were emptied—men shot, women and children marched to death in the Syrian desert—because they were “Armenians.” A weaver crafting rugs, a grandfather telling tales—none mattered; their group condemned them.

Ottoman Muslim officials planned this with precision: roundups, executions, starvation marches. 

Vahé Tachjian, quoting survivor Mariam Mikaelian, recorded: “They took my husband and sons… I begged, ‘They’ve done nothing,’ but they said, ‘You’re all the same.’ We walked until we dropped.” Rivers filled with bodies, babies died in mothers’ arms—all “Armenians,” not people. The Young Turks’ rhetoric cast them as a collective threat, dehumanizing them into targets. Difference, yet again, became slaughter’s prelude.

The Common Denominator: Group Judgmentalism

The Holocaust, slavery, Nanjing, Rwanda, Armenia—what unites these horrors? Group judgmentalism—the act of judging humans by category, not as unique individuals with minds, potentials, lives. Nazis didn’t see a Jewish poet’s verses; slavers ignored an African dancer’s grace; Japanese soldiers dismissed a Chinese elder’s wisdom; Hutus erased a Tutsi mother’s love; Turks silenced an Armenian child’s laughter. Each judged by group—Jews, Africans, Chinese, Tutsis, Armenians—and deemed less human for it. 

Dehumanization followed: “vermin,” “savages,” “pigs,” “cockroaches,” “enemies.” Then murder—six million Jews, millions enslaved, 300,000 in Nanjing, a million Tutsis, 1.5 million Armenians—because difference, judged collectively, kills.

This poison lingers. 

The Holocaust’s group hate stokes Middle East tensions that led to October 7th in Israel. Slavery’s racial judgments fuel America’s divides. Nanjing’s scars strain Sino-Japanese ties. Rwanda’s wounds breed mistrust. Armenia’s memory festers in Muslim Turkey’s denial. Group judgmentalism doesn’t just kill—it scars the future, proving its harm endures.

Whispers of Humanity

Yet amid this carnage, flickers of humanity pierce the gloom—moments where people saw individuals, not groups. In Holocaust-ravaged Poland, farmers hid Jewish families—not “Jews,” but neighbors with names and fears—risking death for their sake. In Denmark, citizens ferried 7,000 Jews to Sweden in fishing boats, seeing friends, not a faceless threat. Oskar Schindler saved 1,200 Jews—not a group, but workers he knew, each a life worth defying the Nazis for. One survivor, Rena Finder, said of Schindler: “He saw us as people, not numbers… he gave us hope.”

During slavery, abolitionists like Frederick Douglass fought for individuals—men and women with stories. Harriet Tubman led hundreds north, seeing souls worth saving. Quakers hid runaways—not “Blacks,” but humans with beating hearts. Solomon Northup, enslaved for 12 years, wrote: “There were moments when I felt a spark of humanity in those who helped me.” In Nanjing, John Rabe sheltered 200,000 Chinese—not a “race,” but people he fed and guarded, defying Japanese blades. A survivor, Xia Shuqin, recalled: “He didn’t see us as Chinese, just as lives to protect.”

In Rwanda, Paul Rusesabagina hid 1,268 Tutsis and Hutus in his hotel—not groups, but individuals he valued. One survivor, Edouard Kayihura, said: “Paul saw me, not my tribe—he saved my life with his heart.” In Armenia, some Turks rescued Armenian neighbors—not “enemies,” but friends they refused to forsake. Survivor Yevnige Salibian recounted: “A Turkish woman hid me… she said, ‘You’re my sister, not their target.’”

These weren’t grand plans—they were instincts breaking through group hate. They saw uniqueness where others saw labels, potential where others saw threats. History whispers: when we see the individual, humanity endures.

The Lesson and the Path

The Holocaust, slavery, Nanjing, Rwanda, Armenia—these aren’t random tragedies but a pattern: judge by group, and you dehumanize; dehumanize, and you destroy. Millions died not for who they were but for what they were called—voices like Levi’s, Jacobs’, Li’s, Ilibagiza’s, Mikaelian’s testify to the loss. The lesson is brutal: group judgmentalism is a poison we can’t afford. Its opposite—seeing each person as a unique individual, equal in humanity—offers hope. Ethical Individualism builds on that truth, a path to a future where harmony replaces slaughter, where we see humans, not groups.

text:
📖 DAILY SCRIPTURE

Birthing of A Nation
Faith • Family • Freedom

TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 10, 2026

WHEN FAITH TEARS THE ROOF OFF!

📖 Mark 2:5 (NLT)

“Seeing their faith, Jesus said to the paralyzed man, ‘My child, your sins are forgiven.’”

🔥 WHEN LOVE REFUSES TO GIVE UP

Imagine being completely helpless, unable to walk, and dependent upon others to carry you wherever you need to go.

Then you hear about Jesus.

The One who heals the sick, restores the broken, and changes lives is nearby!

But there’s a problem.

The house where Jesus is teaching is overflowing with people. The doorway is blocked. There is no room to get through.

For most people, that would have been the end of the journey.

But not for four determined friends.

They didn’t allow the obstacle in front of them to become the end of their faith.

📖 A STORY TO REMEMBER

Picture four men carrying their paralyzed friend through crowded streets.

They finally reach the house, only to discover they cannot get inside.

They could have said, “We tried.”

They could have turned around and carried him home.

Instead, they look up.

The roof!

They climb onto the house, carrying their helpless friend, and begin opening the roof above Jesus.

Imagine the people inside looking up as dust and pieces of roofing begin falling!

Suddenly, a man is being lowered through the ceiling.

Right in front of Jesus!

And Scripture tells us something extraordinary.

Jesus saw THEIR faith!

Not just the faith of the man on the mat, but the faith of those who refused to abandon him.

✝️ JESUS AT THE CENTRE

What happened next was even greater than they expected.

Before Jesus healed the man’s body, He addressed his deepest need.

His sins.

Jesus declared his sins forgiven, then demonstrated His authority by commanding him to rise, pick up his mat, and walk.

The man who had been carried into that house walked out on his own feet!

They brought him to Jesus for healing, but Jesus revealed His authority to forgive sins.

Our greatest need is not simply a change in circumstances.

It is reconciliation with God through Jesus Christ.

🔥 PRACTICAL APPLICATION

How many people around us are spiritually, emotionally, or physically struggling?

Some are too exhausted to keep fighting.

Others have lost hope.

And sometimes they need someone willing to carry them when they cannot carry themselves.

We talk about unity in our families, churches, and communities.

But genuine unity is more than standing together when everything is going well.

It’s refusing to leave someone behind when the journey becomes difficult.

Those four men didn’t compete over who would receive the credit.

They had one mission.

Get their friend to Jesus!

Imagine what our churches would look like if we had that same determination.

🎯 TODAY’S MISSION

Think of someone who is struggling and may have lost the strength to keep going.

Reach out. Pray for them. Offer practical help.

Don’t simply tell them to have more faith.

Be the friend who helps carry them toward Jesus.

🙏 PRAYER

Heavenly Father, give us the faith of those four men. Open our eyes to the hurting and strengthen our willingness to help. Lord Jesus, forgive our sins, restore the broken, and unite Your Church in compassion and truth. Help us never abandon those who need someone to stand beside them. In Jesus’ precious name, Amen.

#BirthingOfANation #DailyScripture #FaithFamilyFreedom #Mark25 #JesusChrist #FaithInAction #CarryOneAnother #NeverGiveUp #ChristianEncouragement #Alberta

"Then we started building our training facility -- Ridge Camp. It was five miles beyond the airport, so we built roads. We built barracks, mess halls, classrooms, armories, and offices. We built a training camp for five thousand and opened it on the fifteenth of January, 1965."
Having put his management team and facilities in place, Donohue next had to demonstrate that the CIA could develop people's action teams for every province, which meant centralized training and using Scotton's forty-man model from Quang Ngai. Donohue also arranged for the training of CTs and Census Grievance cadre. To manage the CT training program, he imported "a couple of guys from headquarters. They were experts. They taught how to get in, how to abduct prisoners, and how to get the hell out with good sources for interrogation. I brought them out TDY and kept talking them into extending, and they both ended up doing a full tour." Both, Donohue said in 1986, "are still gainfully employed by the CIA."
Donohue's pet program was Census Grievance, "the most sophisticated program in the whole goddamned country -- the most effective political tool, if you accept the fact that the government really didn't care what people thought or what their political needs were." Noting that the VC had made the problem worse by cutting the lines of communication, "through the skillful use of terror," Donohue said, "the population had been cut adrift, and Census Grievance was the ersatz system that allowed us to say, 'We accept the fact that there are no normal political lines of influence, so we'll put this on and hope to God we can jump-start this body politic.'"
Donohue explained Census Grievance like this: "Everybody knows the government takes a census, so you'd have a guy make a map of every house in the village -- put everything into perspective. Then the edict was issued that once a month every head of household had to talk to the Census Grievance officer. We tried to get somebody from the village who was older -- retired teachers, retired civil servants -- older people who appeared harmless but were respected." To make it possible for a head of household to speak privately with the Census Grievance officer, "We would put together a little two-by-four shack (patterned on the Catholic confessional) so that there ain't nobody else around.
"Basically the census, scaled down, had three questions: (One) What would you like the GVN to do for you? All of the basic precinct-type needs. 'A bridge across this particular canal would save us a three-mile walk to get our produce to market.' Very legitimate needs. (Two) Is there anybody in the GVN giving you a hard time? Are the police at the checkpoint charging you a toll every time you take your rutabagas to market? (Three) Is there anything you want to tell me about the Vietcong? If the answer was no, the whole thing wasn't pursued, but once a month the head of household had to touch base. If the Census Grievance officer finds that X number of people say they need a bridge, you begin to get a consensus. Okay, money is allocated. If it went to the wrong things, you might as well keep it back here. So the point we would make with the province and district chiefs was 'This is a political need. If you are responsive to it, people will look at you in a different light.'"
35
"Census Grievance produced a good bit of intelligence," Donohue concluded. "So did the cadre program. But there were areas that were so tough and so inaccessible that there was just no intelligence coming out. Some of the Chieu Hois would bring it in, but we never really had what we thought was a good enough handle on continuing intelligence, which is a terrible blind spot if you're trying to win a war that's got all the built in problems that Vietnam had."
The next problem Donohue faced was "how to imprint a political system on a foreign country." That was no easy task, even for an irrepressible huckster like Tom Donohue. Donohue described the typical province chief as "a military officer who was a product of a mandarin system," a person with total discretion over how to spend funds, who "couldn't care less about what some grubby little old peasant lady in black pajamas had to say. He didn't have a political bone in his body." By way of comparison he added, "They're as bad as our military. They never understood either what we were doing." All that led Donohue to say, "We were running a coaching school for army officers."
Further complicating things was the fact that corruption in the provinces was a way of life. So Donohue spent a good deal of time "trying to keep the local parties from using it to their own advantage. The VNQDD element had to be goddamned careful that they weren't pushing the long-range interests of the party," he said, referring to Mai's habit of inserting four VNQDD cadres into every PAT team. "The same is true when you get into Hoa Hao country. If you had a province chief who looked upon it as a source of revenue or if a guy wanted to use it as a private army, then you had real trouble."
Donohue told each province chief, "If you use these people in the way they've been trained, we'll feed them, pay them, and equip them. If you decide at any time they're a hindrance rather than a help, you give me a call, and within thirty days we'll get them out of here. If I decide that you're not using them properly -- that you're using them as a palace guard here in the province -- I'll give you thirty days' notice and pull them out." And that was the agreement. It was that simple. Nothing in writing. Nothing went through the central government.
"Next, I'd take an agency officer -- or officers in a big province -- and stick him in the province and tell him, 'Find a place to live. Get some sandbags. We'll try to get you some Nung guards. Stay alive and do as you see fit.' And then he was responsible for the direction of the teams -- payroll, logistics, the whole smear." The CIA officer then selected "a vigorous young lieutenant" whom the province security officer would appoint to his staff as the Rural Construction cadre liaison, "so we would have a guy we could work with day in and day out. Then we would work down to the district level, where we had a similar arrangement, and then into a village."
As soon as the district chief had vouched for his recruits, "We'd put them on an airplane and send them down to Vung Tau," Donohue said. "This is pretty heady stuff. These guys had never been out of the village before. The food was spectacular. Suddenly they had more protein in their systems than they've ever had before, and they're able to stay awake in class. Our training program was vigorous as hell, but they all put on weight. We treated them for worms as soon as they came in the door. Then Mai began telling them stories about the fairies and the dragons and the great cultural heritage of the Vietnamese people. He had all sorts of myths which were at least apparent to many of these people. Then he would work in the political applicability of today."
According to Donohue, this is "precisely" what political warfare is all about: Having been selected into a "special" program and given "special" treatment, CIA political cadres were taught the corporate sales pitch. In effect, rural youths were put on a political assembly line, pumped full of protein and propaganda, cross-trained as interchangeable parts for efficiency, then given one last motivational booster shot. "The graduation ceremonies at Vung Tau were something else." Donohue chortled. "At night. Total darkness. Then the one candle lit. Oh! This is the schmaltz! Remember, these are kids that have never seen anything like this. The pageantry!"
The New York Times reporter R.W. Apple described on February 21, 1965 the Ridge Camp graduation ceremony occurring in an amphitheater the size of a football field. Filipino trainers were present and, writes Apple, "The ceremony had a theatrical, almost religious quality. Vietnamese national symbols, including the old imperial flag, were arrayed before an altar. Multi-colored pennants bearing the names of the nation's ancient heroes were mounted behind the speaker. Captain Mai stood at an illuminated lectern. The recruits were grouped on the three other sides of the arena. At a signal, all the lights except one focused on Captain Mai went out, and the recruits stripped off their white shirts and dark trousers. When the lights came on again, all were clad in black pajamas."
Whipped into an ideological fervor, the CIA's political cadres were then sent into villages to spread democratic values and undermine the infrastructure.
"It's a GVN presence that's really comprised of your own people that have, by God, gone off and been washed in the blood of the lamb. They've been trained and they've seen the light," Donohue palavered.
36
"They spoke the local dialect, and they're there to defend and focus people on their own defense, to try to enlist the people into doing something positive. If the government can't protect you, it ain't no government."
Of course, the GVN was not a government but a military dictatorship which was opposed to independence in the countryside. The GVN at that time, writes Professor Huy, "could be curiously compared to that of the USSR with the Armed Forces Council as the Supreme Soviet, the Committee Leading the Nation as its Presidium, and the Central Executive Committee as the Soviet government before World War Two when its ministers were called commissars. General Nguyen Van Thieu was elected chairman of the Committee Leading the Nation and so became chief of state. General Nguyen Cao Ky was appointed chairman of the Central Executive Committee, i.e. the government." [9]
In June 1965 the National Council of Security was created and placed under Ky, who reported to Thieu but in fact exercised greater power than Thieu. As prime minister controlling the Interior Ministry, Ky appointed his people to the CIA 's covert action program and appointed his confidential agent, General Nguyen Ngoc Loan, director of the Military Security Service in June 1965, director general of the National Police in October 1965, and head of the Central Intelligence Organization in Apri1 1966.
Explains Huy:
Nguyen Cao Ky was strongly backed by the Americans anxious to find a leader for the Vietnamese. A program called Rural Development, later called the Phoenix program, was set up. It aimed at detecting and destroying the communist cells in villages and reconstructing the countryside. This program was undertaken with means provided by the USA. It was smaller than what we had tried to apply when Nguyen Ton Roan was deputy prime minister in charge of Pacification. The only difference was that now, the personnel in use were not politically motivated and trained cadres, but merely dispirited employees of the government. [10]
Frank Scotton was also critical of Vung Tau. "I shied away from Vung Tau," he said, "because the American hand became too big and because having a fixed complex was spiritually uncomfortable. Spiritually the thing to do was to go into the villages. At Vung Tau they were not dealing with unconventional warfare, but with warehousers. There was always the threat that 'We'll turn off the water' if you don't do it our way." [11]
He also criticized the "development of incantation and rote" and the resulting "doctrinaire" mind-set that led to the Rural Construction program's being compared with Hitler's Strength Through Joy camps. Its cadre studied the ninety-eight duties, the eleven-point criteria, and the twelve phases of action. They sang the "New Life Hamlet Construction" song, with its symbolic twelve stanzas and ninety-eight notes, and recited the ritual Five Oaths: "Standing before the altar of our Fatherland and the national Flag, we, in the capacity of rural construction cadres, take the oath ... to remain faithful ... to firmly believe ... that cadres are created by the people ... to mingle with the people ... and to make constant efforts in study in order to progress in behavior, education and techniques." [12]
Scotton's biggest complaint, however, was the shift from intelligence and displacement to civic action. The change took place in early 1965, when Robert Kelly joined the CIA and took his team of instructors to duplicate the Quang Ngai program in other provinces. At that point Harry "The Hat" Monk took over in Binh Dinh Province and began working as case officer to Major Nguyen Be, the former insurgent who, before defecting, had been party secretary for the Ninth Vietcong Battalion. A visionary, Be wanted Rural Construction to be more than an attack on the VCI; he wanted to provide services to the people as well. Perceiving the PATs as "too American," he retrained his people as they returned to Binh Dinh from Vung Tau and, with the help of Monk, combined "mobile" Census Grievance cadres, PATs, and CTs, and came up with the fifty-nine-man Revolutionary Development (RD) team.
Be's fifty-nine-man RD teams had group leaders and psywar, intelligence, and medical specialists in staff positions. There were three eleven-man teams constituting an "action element" and having a counterterror mission, and there was a Rural Construction leader with a six-man Civic Action team; a six-man "mobile" Census Grievance team under the intelligence office; and a six-man economic unit. Be's teams were called Purple People Eaters by American soldiers, in reference to their clothes and terror tactics. To the rural Vietnamese they were simply "idiot birds."
Said Scotton: "Be was trying to create a climate to make the VC blunder into ambushes and fear the unpredictable." His goal was to neutralize the VC, but his style was "be nice to VC agents, give them gifts, smother them with affection, and then let them try to explain that to their superiors." It was a style Scotton did not approve of, although he loved Be himself. "Be was like an older brother to me and an uncle to my children," Scotton said. "He lived with us from 1976 until he died in summer of 1981."
37
Despite Scotton's compunctions, by mid-1965 the CIA was using Be's fifty-nine-man model as its standard team, at which point the Rural Construction Cadre program was renamed the Revolutionary Development Cadre program. With larger teams and standardization came the need for more advisers, so Donohue began recruiting military men like Joe Vacarro, a Special Forces sergeant working as a Public Safety adviser in Quang Nam Province. "I met Joe and chatted with him," Donohue said, "and he looked interesting, so I went to AID, and he was sort of seconded to me; although he still worked for AID, I wrote his fitness reports. Then I worked out a direct hire for him, and he came back here to D.C., did some formal Vietnamese training, then went back out for another tour." Vaccaro was to become heavily involved in the Provincial Reconnaissance Unit training program at Vung Tau. Donohue also hired Jean Sauvageot out of the Army. Sauvageot was to become the scion of Vung Tau and a close aide to Frank Scotton, his mentor, and William Colby.
"We get to the point," according to Donohue, "where the CIA was running a political program in a sovereign country where they didn't know what the hell we were teaching. So I had Thieu and Ky down to Vung Tau, and I did all the right things. But what kind of program could it be that had only one sponsor, the CIA, that says it was doing good? It had to be sinister. Any red-blooded American could understand that. What the hell is the CIA doing running a program on political action?
"So I went out to try to get some cosponsors for the record. They weren't easy to come by. I went to [USIS chief] Barry Zorthian. I said, 'Barry, how about giving us someone?' I talked to MACV about getting an officer assigned. I had AID give me a guy." But most of it, Donohue said, "was window dressing. We had the funds; we had the logistics; we had the transportation."
The CIA also had the approbation of Ky and Thieu. "Ky and Thieu saw the wisdom of it," Donohue said, "so they offered up (as their liaison to the program) General Nguyen Duc Thang. And he was indefatigable. He went everyplace." There was, however, one catch. As a way of monitoring the Saigon station, in August 1965 the Special Group assigned Ed Lansdale as senior liaison to General Thang, who instantly advocated transferring the entire Revolutionary Development program to the Defense Ministry.
"Ed Lansdale was an invention of Hubert Humphrey's," Donohue grumbled. "The idea was 'We did it before, we can do it again.' So Lansdale came out two years too late. He brought a lot of his old cohorts; some were agency guys that he'd suborned. He had some Army people and some retired folks, but there was really nothing," Donohue said wearily, "for them to do."
"My boss [Gordon Jorgenson, who replaced Peer DeSilva in February 1965] said, 'Tell them everything.' I said okay, and I spent two and a half hours briefing his full group about a week after they arrived. And they said, 'Let's have a joint office.' So we had our logistics people put in offices and all the right things. Then I had to get somebody to run the office. Thang said, 'Who do you want?' And I said, 'Chau.'"
Tran Ngoc Chau, according to Donohue, "was a farsighted, bright guy with an ability to keep meaningful statistics -- which is not very Vietnamese. He'd been the apple of Diem's eye during the strategic hamlet program, and he had a special phone to the palace -- Diem was on the horn to him constantly. Because he had that kind of sponsorship, he was able to do an awful lot of experimentation. So we used Kien Hoa as a proving ground. I spent a lot of time between Mai and Chau looking at programs," Donohue recalled, "trying to introduce refinements."
By having Chau transferred to Vung Tau, Donohue also got greater control over his pet project. "We took Census Grievance and expanded it," he said. "I got a villa in Gia Dinh and set up a training school for Census Grievance people. We would bring people in that had been spotted in various villages and run them through the training; then they would go back to their provinces. I had a French gent, Matisse, who ran the school. We trained in small groups, and it was a much faster process than the PATs; but these were literate people, so they were quick on the uptake. And it was very pleasant surroundings. It was a well-handled program." To it Donohue assigned John O'Reilly, John Woodsman, Dick Fortin, and Jean Sauvageot.
"But I had forced the transfer," Donohue confessed, "and Chau was so damn mad that he was in a permanent pout. So he decided to go down to Vung Tau and shape the place up. Which we really didn't need. 'Cause here you have two dynamic personalities [Mai and Chau] who couldn't stand each other."
The conflict was resolved in 1966, when Mai was reassigned to the Joint General Staff, while Chau took over the Vung Tau training program. Donohue minimized the effect. "I couldn't really do much business out there anyway," he noted, "because I needed our own system to talk to people. But at least for the record it looked pretty good. We had a MAVC guy, an AID guy, and a USIS guy down at Vung Tau, so all the bases had been touched. You see," he added, "at this point all we were trying to do was expand the thing and say that there's at least plausible denial that the agency is solely responsible."
38
Indeed, with the creation of Vung Tau and the synthetic Revolutionary Development Cadre program, South Vietnam began slouching toward democracy. But it was an empty gesture. The rule in South Vietnam was one step forward followed by two steps back.

Marshall Smith (former Alberta Premier Danielle Smith’s Chief of Staff) rose from addiction and homelessness on Vancouver’s Downtown Eastside to shape Alberta’s recovery-focused “Alberta Model.”
Recruited by then-Premier Jason Kenney in 2019 after BC rejected his recovery proposals, he drove a shift toward residential treatment communities. He has long credited Vancouver police officers who offered him treatment-or-jail with helping save his life; he has been in recovery since the late 2000s.
Later reporting linked him to businessman Sam Mraiche (including living in a home owned by Mraiche’s sister and hiring several Mraiche relatives into government roles) amid ongoing procurement investigations and lawsuits. Smith has denied wrongdoing

The conversation about higher education consolidation should continue. But it should begin with the right question.

A new Signal Ohio article examines whether Ohio’s public colleges and universities should pursue greater consolidation, collaboration, and systemwide transformation as enrollment, workforce needs, infrastructure costs, and financial pressures change.

The question should not simply be:

How many institutions should Ohio have?

It should be:

How can Ohio’s institutions work together more effectively to serve students, strengthen academic programs, meet workforce needs, and steward public resources?

In the article, @HCSStrategy founder @BrianWeinblatt emphasizes an important distinction between structural change developed by institutions and change imposed upon them.

As Brian told @SignalOhio:

“It’s that whole notion of having something done to you or having something done by you.”

The 2006 merger of The University of Toledo and the Medical University of Ohio offers one useful example. The combination brought together complementary strengths and emerged from institutional leadership rather than a predetermined mandate to reduce the number of campuses.

State leaders can help create incentives, provide transition resources, reduce regulatory barriers, and develop a broader vision for public higher education. But durable transformation requires institutional ownership, trust, careful planning, and a compelling academic and public-purpose rationale.

The consolidation conversation should continue. It should also focus on better outcomes, not simply fewer institutions.

Xbox Consoles Overview

The Xbox Series X is Microsoft's flagship console, designed for true 4K gaming and featuring a disc drive, while the Xbox Series S is a more compact, digital-only alternative targeting 1440p resolution.

Playstation

The PlayStation 5 (PS5) is Sony's current generation of home video game consoles, available in standard (disc) and Digital Editions, as well as a more powerful Pro model released in November 2024. The original launch models have been replaced by slimmer hardware revisions.

Key Features

Immersive Experience: Both models offer breathtaking 4K visuals (up to 120fps on compatible games) and the Tempest Engine for hardware-accelerated 3D Audio effects.

DualSense Controller: Features haptic feedback (realistic physical sensations) and adaptive triggers (dynamic resistance) for deeper immersion.

Ultra-High Speed SSD: A custom solid-state drive allows for lightning-fast loading times, enabling game developers to design vast worlds with near-instant data streaming.

Backward Compatibility: The PS5 is compatible with the vast majority of PlayStation 4 games, many of which benefit from faster and smoother frame rates with Game Boost technology.

PS5 Pro Enhancements: The Pro model features a faster GPU (about 45% faster), improved ray tracing, and AI-driven upscaling technology (PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution or PSSR).

CM Punk is the official cover star for the Standard Edition.

WWE 2K26

Key Details and Platforms

The game is being developed by Visual Concepts and published by 2K. It will not be released on last-generation consoles (PS4, Xbox One), focusing exclusively on current generation hardware.

Developer: Visual Concepts

Publisher: 2K

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Windows PC (via Steam), and Nintendo Switch 2

New Features

WWE 2K26 promises a range of new features and improvements across its game modes, including the largest roster in franchise history with over 400 Superstars and Legends.

New Match Types: Additions include I Quit, Inferno, Dumpster, and Three Stages of Hell matches.

2K Showcase: Punked: A career-spanning story mode focused on CM Punk, featuring a mix of historical matches and "fantasy warfare" scenarios, narrated by Punk himself.

Roster: Features over 400 playable characters, including current Superstars and Legends such as The Rock, Triple H, John Cena, and CM Punk.

MyGM Mode: Expanded to support more match types (intergender, 5, 6, and 8-man matches) and additional brands.

Universe Mode: The WWE Draft is integrated into this sandbox mode, along with new promo types and a "Watch Show" spectator option.

Pro Wrestling Manager/Advovate/GOAT Paul Heyman On WWE2K26

“I appreciate the question and I understand where it’s coming from, but if I were to do that, then I’m living my own fantasy within the video game and I don’t know if you are aware of this, I am maybe a couple of weeks, months, maybe even a year or two older than the typical gamer that’s out there today.

“So because of that I try not to play to my own fantasy booking, I try to play to the audience’s fantasy booking, and not just the WWE audience, but the video game audience itself. ‘Cause I would like to steal people from other video game franchises. I like to entice people to not play Fortnite, but to play WWE 2k26. I would like to entice people to not play Call of Duty, but to play WWE 2k26.

“So it’s not just a matter of, ‘Ooh, what would happen if I put Lou Thesz and Bruno Sammartino and Brock Lesnar in a triple threat match together?’ It’s more of, ‘What can appeal to today’s gamer audience? What appeals to that crowd? Hash 🍯🥭🍈: Rambutan #11 (1 gram) (Cold Cure) (Persy Rosin) by @710labs 

Genetics🧬: Papaya x Guavaz #74

Setup: Reverendmorse (Rig), @jptoroglass Slurper XL (Nail), Highly Educated (Pillar), Black Zach Brown (Slurper Cap), @TheDabRite (Temp Reader), Disorderly Conduction (Heating Element)

Temp 🌡️: 515°F

🎵: Rambutan by Katon Wazabi

Appearance 👀: The appearance of this jar was nice, opening up to a pale buttery yellow color with a glistening, wet and terpy look to it. The consistency was also good, when I dipped my dab tool into it it had a nice wet terpy consistency that was easy to scoop onto my dab tool without falling off like a dry one would. The jar was also visually clean, with no contaminants visible to the naked eye or even under my phone’s macro lens. 

As for the packaging, the rosin came in a black magnetic closure box featuring a cool design along with the @710labs logo and design. The box also included information about the jar, such as the consistency (Persy Badder), strain name (Rambutan #11), genetics (Papaya x Guavaz #74), package date (09/03/2026), and net weight (1 gram), along with some other additional details. When opening the magnetic box, you're greeted with a black pop-vac jar featuring 710 Labs on the lid, with a sticker on the bottom displaying the consistency, strain name, batch number, and net weight. 8.9/10

Aroma 👃: The aroma on this jar was great. The moment you crack it open, you're hit with a loud burst of tropical sweetness along with a rotten fruit funk that practically jumps out of the jar. You really get those fruity guavaz terps coming through first, followed by the papaya terps, which bring a rotten fruit funk that pairs together nicely. 8.7/10

Taste 👅: The taste on this jar translated incredibly well from the aroma, coming through almost identically on the dab. When you start dabbing, you get a nice tropical fruit sweetness before transitioning into a heavier rotten fruit funk. The two profiles complement each other really well. It's almost like biting into a sweet, juicy mango before getting hit with the taste of some overripe, rotten fruit. 8.6/10

Burn/Smoothness 🧼: The rosin dabbed clean on the nail leaving behind a light golden translucent color, and not a dark or murky color which would indicate there's quite a bit of contaminants. It also dabbed smooth and clean with no background noise when dabbing at my usual temp around 515°F. However when testing out higher temps it did have a bit of a bite but nothing worth complaining about. 8.8/10

Effects 😄: The effects were solid, making this a great daytime jar. They weren’t overly intense, but instead offered a mellow, balanced experience that I really enjoyed. It’s perfect for socializing and staying relaxed without feeling too overly potent. 8.4/10

Overall 📝: This jar from @710labs was solid, and I really enjoyed it. The main reason I picked it up was because I've always enjoyed a well done rambutan, and it had been quite some time since I'd last had this one from @710labs. Since I don't have easy access to it living outside of California, I figured I'd take the opportunity to grab it while I could at Puffcon. Unfortunately, they weren't storing the hash in a cooler at the event, they had it sitting in boxes with the sun beating down on them, which definitely wasn't ideal. Surprisingly, though, the rosin still held up pretty well and wasn't bad at all considering the conditions.  Another reason I got this jar is because I enjoy comparing the recreational market to the traditional market and seeing how the quality stacks up. Last reason is I'm hoping to get my hands on this same strain from Keeping It Coastal, so I thought it would be interesting to compare the two. Although they aren't the exact same cut, they're both Rambutan, so it'll still be a cool comparison.

@710labs is a California based recreational market cannabis brand that actually started in Colorado and has been on the market since 2010. The brand specializes in small batch, organically grown cannabis, solventless extracts (such as live rosin, water hash, and sauce) but also flower, vape pods, pre-rolled "doinks" (with fusilli noodle filters), and hash rosin edibles. Their concentrates and products are categorized into quality tiers (from Persy to Tier 4). The brand is usually all in house but they do collabs sometimes with some in the past being with Alien Labs, Fear of Boof, Lazercat and a couple others. 

This jar checked pretty much all the boxes for me. The looks, aroma, taste, burn/smoothness, and effects were all enjoyable, making for a really solid overall experience from start to finish. I really enjoyed the tropical fruit profile paired with those heavier rotten, funky notes, and it was nice to see that the flavor translated so well from the aroma into the dab.

@710labs did a great job with this jar, which comes as no surprise considering they’re one of the best recreational hash brands on the market. This jar was genuinely impressive, especially when you take the pricing into consideration. I typically pay more on the traditional market side of things, so it was nice to see this level of quality available at a more accessible price point. I wouldn’t necessarily call it anything mind blowing, but it was still some damn good hash. That said, I’d personally still give the traditional market the edge in overall quality, but that’s just my take. I would also definitely get this jar at that price and quality it’s hard to say no as I usually pay more so. Shoutout to @710labs! 8.6/10

text:
$MAMESUKE (CA: SCGBBnSwnekytGFHgyeHHxPMiN7xDxsWFGg9JgFSTNK) Since Launch (Based on On-chain Data & X/Twitter)

Token Background
$MAMESUKE is a Solana-based meme coin that launched around November 2, 2026, via StonkFun / Raydium LaunchLab. It subsequently graduated to the Raydium CPMM (primarily paired with STONK) and is also available in liquidity pools such as those on Meteora. The token’s narrative centers on "Mamesuke"—a real-life Shiba Inu mascot featured in the long-running TV Osaka program *Wafu Sōhonke* (Japanese Tradition Headquarters). Known for wearing a green *karakusa* (arabesque-patterned) bandana, the character has appeared on the show since 2008 and returned to television in October 2026 (as the 26th generation). The show airs every other Tuesday, with related video clips garnering millions, and sometimes tens of millions, of views. The official description reads: "The Japanese Icon. Airing every other Tuesday." Mint and freeze authorities have been revoked; however, the liquidity lock ratio is relatively low (approximately 41%), resulting in a "Caution" flag. The token has around 5,000 holders, with a current market cap generally in the $450,000–$500,000 range, often experiencing 24-hour declines of around 40%. Its all-time high (ATH) is reported to have been in the $2.7 million–$3.2 million range.

Price Trajectory Overview
Launch Day (November 2): An explosive surge occurred, with the market cap climbing rapidly from near-zero to hundreds of thousands—and eventually millions—of dollars. The token saw gains of several thousand percent within 24 hours, accompanied by trading volume in the millions of dollars.
November 3: The price continued to climb, closing the day even higher, with the market cap peaking near or above $2 million–$3 million (figures vary by source, but a significant ATH is clear).
Subsequent Period: The price has largely retreated from its highs, characterized by significant volatility. It has pulled back by over 80% from its ATH to current levels; while there have been occasional rebounds, the overall trend remains clearly downward. High trading volume has been accompanied by heavy selling pressure. Sasapad
Primary Drivers for the Price Surge
Strong Narrative and Timing: Based on an authentic Japanese television IP with an established, long-term audience—bolstered by a recent revival and the airing of new episodes (including one on November 3rd)—the project benefited from viral video content that facilitated organic spread. Unlike "memes" created from scratch, this offered a more compelling "real-world" backstory.
Social Catalysts on X (Influencers/Key Accounts):
A major account, WhaleInsider, reported that the official Shiba Inu account followed the project, and noted that Elon Musk "liked" a reply mentioning "$MAMESUKE shiba."
KOLs like @DaCryptoGeneral hyped the project, calling it a "cult" and predicting it would "send it to 10M" [market cap].
Early promotion within the Chinese-speaking community, bidding activity from the "Dabal Club," participation by "STONK" whales, and a community-wide emphasis on the project's viral potential.
These factors amplified FOMO (Fear Of Missing Out), driving a wave of speculative buying.
Early On-Chain Buying: High trading volume and an influx of buyers immediately following the launch rapidly pushed up the market capitalization. The StonkFun platform itself also garnered a certain level of attention.
Primary Reasons for the Price Decline (Core Factors)
Highly Structured On-Chain "Farming/Bundling" Sell-off (The Critical Factor): A detailed analysis by Phoenix Reports reveals that a master wallet (Ek1Z…MXWu) funded the creator, purchasing approximately 79% of the total supply at the genesis block. This supply was concealed within a one-sided Meteora DLMM liquidity pool—meaning it did not appear in standard "holder" lists—and was subsequently liquidated through 18 rotating operational wallets (executing ~1,868 sell transactions, offloading over 435 million tokens, and cashing out more than $200,000 worth of STONK). Persistent sell pressure existed throughout the price rally, ultimately resulting in a massive cashing out into SOL. Other tactics included the siphoning of creator fees and the distribution of tokens to "fake" holders. This is a classic "insider-led" dump, where external buyers effectively provided the exit liquidity.
Profit-Taking + Thin Liquidity: Natural profit-taking occurred after the asset reached an all-time high (ATH). Given the limited depth of the liquidity pool (typically ranging from $50,000 to $130,000), large or consecutive sell orders easily triggered significant slippage and price drops. 24-hour trading volume is significant, but selling pressure at higher price levels dominates.
Narrative and social momentum have waned, compounded by market noise:
Initial interest was driven by associations with SHIB and posts mentioning Elon Musk, but the project lacked sustained, powerful catalysts.
The existence of multiple tokens sharing the same or similar names (including an earlier version on https://t.co/FC6yCRySNU) led to debates over which was the "OG" (original) versus a "fake," causing a fragmentation of interest.
On X (formerly Twitter), the discourse shifted toward aggressive shilling, "vote-to-claim" airdrop scams, and FUD (fear, uncertainty, and doubt) regarding "farming" or "bundling" tactics. There was no sustained, high-conviction backing from prominent influencers (KOLs).
Other on-chain characteristics: The top 10 holders account for a moderate concentration (approx. 17–21%), and the low percentage of locked liquidity (LP) heightens perceived risk. While there was no classic "mint/freeze" rug pull, the supply was clearly controlled by specific entities from the outset.
Summary
Upside: Driven primarily by the narrative of a real-life Japanese TV mascot, favorable timing (the show’s return to air), and FOMO-fueled buying amplified by KOLs (such as WhaleInsider, Crypto General, etc.) and the community.
Downside: Primarily driven by the fact that the dominant on-chain actors controlled the vast majority of the supply from the start and systematically offloaded their holdings during the price rally (a "farming" model). This was compounded by profit-taking at higher levels, thin liquidity, and the fading of key catalysts. This follows a common pattern seen in early-stage Solana meme coins: a "narrative-driven surge" followed by an "exit by the supply-controlling entities"—rather than an external "black swan" event or a sudden, outright abandonment by the project team.

CENTRAL ARWX STORM CENTER | MONDAY EVENING, NOVEMBER 9, 2026
Good evening, Central Arkansas!

We've got quite a bit to discuss in tonight's forecast! From a beautiful stretch of fall weather to our first widespread freeze of the season, and now increasing signs of a much more active weather pattern heading toward Thanksgiving!

AND THAT MAY NOT BE THE ONLY THING WE'RE WATCHING! 👀

Let's break it all down!

🌙 TONIGHT'S FORECAST — CLEAR & COOL!

We're expecting another quiet November night across Central Arkansas with mostly clear to partly cloudy skies and cool temperatures.

Most communities will drop into the lower and middle 40s, with some of our cooler valleys falling into the upper 30s.

🌡️ TONIGHT'S FORECAST LOWS:

🥶 Clinton: 40°
🥶 Russellville: 41°
🥶 Conway: 42°
🥶 Benton: 43°
🥶 Hot Springs: 45°
🥶 Little Rock: 45°

No widespread frost or freezing temperatures are expected tonight.
☀️ THE WEEK AHEAD — ENJOY THE WARMTH WHILE IT LASTS!
We're looking at another beautiful stretch of fall weather through midweek before a much stronger cold front changes things heading toward the weekend!
📅 YOUR CENTRAL ARWX 7-DAY FORECAST
🌤️ TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 10: Mostly cloudy to partly sunny skies with mild temperatures. High 71° | Low 53°.
🌤️ VETERANS DAY WEDNESDAY: Partly cloudy and warm! High 76° | Low 45°. A very slight 10% chance of an isolated shower.
☀️ THURSDAY: Sunny, breezy, and turning cooler behind our next cold front! High 64° | Low 35°.
🥶 FRIDAY: Turning noticeably colder! Sunshine continues, but afternoon highs struggle to reach the middle 50s. High 54° | Low 31°.
❄️ SATURDAY: A FREEZING START TO THE WEEKEND! Sunny skies with highs near 57° after a very cold morning. Overnight low near 34°.
☀️ SUNDAY: Partly cloudy with temperatures slowly recovering. High 59° | Low 39°.

🌤️ MONDAY: Partly cloudy and milder, with highs near 62° and lows around 40°.

🚨🥶 FIRST WIDESPREAD FREEZE OF THE SEASON EXPECTED FRIDAY NIGHT INTO SATURDAY MORNING!

THIS continues to be our biggest short-term weather story!

A strong cold front moving through Arkansas later this week will allow much colder air to settle across the region heading into Saturday morning.

Our latest temperature guidance continues to show widespread lower 30s, with several locations potentially falling BELOW FREEZING!
AND I STILL BELIEVE SOME OF THIS GUIDANCE MAY BE A TOUCH TOO WARM!

If skies clear and winds become light Friday night, temperatures could fall several degrees below current projections.
That could result in freezing temperatures becoming more widespread than the current forecast suggests.

🌱 NOW IS THE TIME TO START THINKING ABOUT PROTECTING SENSITIVE PLANTS!
A widespread frost is looking increasingly likely, and many communities may experience their first freeze of the fall season.

🦌 MODERN GUN DEER SEASON OPENING WEEKEND!
For our Arkansas deer hunters, opening morning Saturday could be COLD!

Temperatures near or below freezing are possible across much of Central Arkansas around sunrise.

The good news? We're currently expecting dry weather with plenty of sunshine throughout the day.
So grab those heavier jackets if you're heading into the woods early Saturday morning!

🌡️ BUT HERE'S SOMETHING IMPORTANT — THIS COLD SHOT LOOKS BRIEF!

While temperatures will drop significantly late this week, the cold air doesn't appear likely to stick around for an extended period.

We're expecting temperatures to gradually moderate Sunday into early next week.

And that temporary warmup could become important as our next weather systems begin to take shape!

🌧️ NOW LET'S TALK ABOUT SOMETHING WE DESPERATELY NEED... RAIN!

We've been discussing the ongoing drought across Arkansas for weeks, and unfortunately, the upcoming seven-day forecast doesn't offer much meaningful rainfall.

But beyond that?

THINGS ARE STARTING TO LOOK A LITTLE MORE INTERESTING! 👀🌧️

Our longer-range forecast guidance is beginning to show increasing opportunities for rainfall during the second half of November.

The latest Climate Prediction Center outlook also highlights portions of Central Arkansas with a Slight Risk of heavy precipitation during the November 16–22 period.

This doesn't guarantee a heavy rainfall event, but it's another indication that we may finally be moving toward a more active weather pattern.

🌧️ LATE NEXT WEEK — OUR NEXT POTENTIAL WEATHER MAKER!

Our extended forecast currently shows scattered shower chances returning around Thursday, November 19.

And we're continuing to monitor additional potential systems beyond that timeframe!

Could this finally bring some much-needed widespread rainfall to Arkansas?

IT'S POSSIBLE, BUT WE STILL HAVE SOME WORK TO DO BEFORE WE CAN GET EXCITED ABOUT SPECIFIC RAINFALL TOTALS!

The exact timing, track, and intensity of these systems remain uncertain.

🦃🥶 AND THEN THERE'S THANKSGIVING WEEK...

Here's where the longer-range forecast starts getting REALLY interesting!

Some guidance is beginning to suggest the possibility of ANOTHER SUBSTANTIAL SHOT OF COLD AIR as we approach Thanksgiving.

And depending on how the larger-scale weather pattern evolves, additional precipitation opportunities may also become possible.

COULD WE BE LOOKING AT AN EVEN BIGGER PATTERN CHANGE AS NOVEMBER COMES TO AN END?! 👀

It's simply too early to know.

All revisionist history nonsense. Nebraska was officially talking to the Big 10 in early 2010 (unofficially for years prior) after the Big 10 ANNNOUNCED they were planning on expanding. The pac 10 was targeting 6 schools in June 2010 and only Colorado agreed to leave. Of course Texas didn’t initiate any of this. The Longhorn network wasn’t announced until 2011 long after A&M had been in talks with the SEC and they didn’t leave because of it. Texas had originally offered A&M part of a Lone Star network, but the Aggies declined.  

The Big 12 was never a threat to the SEC and the Big Ten. The conference only had two marquee national brands and there weren’t enough TVs in the other markets to keep it viable. Nebraska, Texas A&M, Colorado and Missouri all left for the same reason. They got more money and more perceived stability because it was clear to everybody - including your school who was more than happy to ride Texas’s coattails to a new destination - that the Big 12 was unsustainable. 

It isn’t Texas’s responsibility to try to prop up some farcical idea of balance just so we could take road trips to Morgantown or Houston for a fraction of our worth. The reality is that at the time at least 10 of the 12 teams were actively working on new homes before the Longhorn Network was even announced.  But everybody has to blame Texas because they’re idiots.

Carny Island: Media and Online News Buzz

Brett Clements is an Australian artist, writer, filmmaker, and game designer best known as the creator of the cult hybrid video board game franchise Nightmare / ATMOSFEAR (which sold over 4 million units).

Carny Island Overview

• Concept: Carny Island is a hybrid video board game and digital experience that mixes physical tabletop play with mobile phones used as interactive entertainment portals.
• Gameplay: Players scavenge graves for body parts and loot to build their own Frankenstein-style creation while trying to survive characters like Uncle Shrift. • Production Team: Developed alongside the team at Mongril Labs, with AI tools supporting coding, testing, and production, and a reunion with former Roadshow Entertainment president Milt Barlow for global licensing.
• Engine/Media: Built using development transitions into Godot, documented via regular dev logs and updates on the Carny Island Official Website and Carny Island YouTube Channel.

Background & Career • Media & Television: A multi-decade veteran across Australian television, network advertising, and journalism, having worked on projects like Simon Townsend's Wonder World! and A Couple 'A Cowboys.
• Other Projects: Involved in producing and directing various digital, real-estate, and documentary ventures, including the guerrilla-shot docu-series SQUAD.
• Online Profiles: You can follow his ongoing production logs via Brett Clements' Portfolio or his LinkedIn Newsletter

*Media Man Group is officially representing (b2b and Media/Online Media/Business Development) Carny Island
